journey: MVP M2: senior resident finds a textile repair clinic

inputs.purpose: Prototype requirements M2.1 and M2.2, screens 5 and 6
Official Boston component and visual guidance
Existing React, TypeScript, Vite, and TanStack Router boundaries
Prompts for clear code, plain explanations, and a contributor demonstration

constraints: Create issues and pull requests in hwillGIT/boston-circular-economy. Upstream issues are reference material.
Use the current textile MVP, a 390-pixel mobile viewport, and Fleet conventions.
Treat the older television persona and technical prototypes as historical context.
Use two synthetic clinics. Do not infer that the backend supports the mock fields.
Separate source facts, AI suggestions, and unresolved decisions.
Do not implement production code, query paid APIs, collect personal data, or publish to Slack.
Use the developer guide for clear code and plain explanations. Reserve the last 15 minutes for explaining and defending the result.
title: Apply a modern Fleet visual treatment
objective: Produce one polished clinic-results screen that preserves the approved interaction and Boston identity.
in_scope: Typography, spacing, hierarchy, and Fleet component mapping

ai_steps.prompt: Use the selected UI-003 wireframe, the MVP, and inspected Fleet sources. Suggest two visual treatments using the existing Boston vocabulary. Compare hierarchy, density, readability, and maintenance in 200 words. Do not introduce a new brand or invent design tokens.

After I select a treatment, create one editable polished 390-pixel screen and a PNG preview. Preserve all information and actions. Use at least 16-pixel body text, clear grouping, and explicit selected/focus states. List the source of each font, color, spacing value, and component; label proposals.

Audit the rendered screen against the accepted wireframe. Check text clipping, hierarchy, contrast measurements, focus visibility, and whether partial-match meaning survives without color. Report observed results and limitations. Do not claim accessibility compliance from an image or AI opinion.

Ask me to explain how the visual choices help a resident compare clinics. Ask which Fleet reference supports each important choice. Ask why I rejected the closest alternative. Increase the content length and ask me to predict the layout. If code exists, ask me to locate the component, token, or style that controls the result. Check my answer against the artifact and measured evidence. Wait for my answers. Do not write my defense for me.

deliverables.name: clinic-results-visual
deliverables.format: Editable design link or self-contained HTML, plus PNG
deliverables.contents: One polished results screen at 390 pixels.

deliverables.name: visual-manifest.yaml
deliverables.contents: Component/style source mapping, sizes, states, measured checks, and approved design revision.

deliverables.name: visual-review.md
deliverables.contents: At most 300 words with checks, trade-offs, and human review.

deliverables.name: contributor-explanation
deliverables.contents: Own explanation of the example, decision, alternative, evidence, failure behavior, and place to make a likely change.

acceptance: The rendered screen retains the accepted content and actions.
Body text is at least 16 pixels and no content clips at 390 pixels.
Fonts, colors, and components trace to Fleet or an explicitly reviewed exception.
The contributor records contrast measurements and keyboard/focus annotations without claiming a full audit.
The design owner approves the visual revision before implementation tickets use it.
The contributor explains the result in their own words and answers one changed-case question from the reviewer.
If the artifact contains code, the contributor locates the input, decision owner, visible result, and supporting behavior check.
Names, types, and boundaries expose any generated code's purpose. Comments preserve reasons that the code cannot express.
The explanation defines unfamiliar terms and states the evidence, limits, and condition for reconsidering the decision.
learning_check: Explain one visual choice in terms of readability or task completion rather than taste. Explain the choice in your own words. Support it with inspected evidence and answer one changed-case question.
handoff: Hubert uses the approved screen and component mapping to shape a small implementation issue.
